item.title: Unauthorized Device Command and Control
item.description: The exported activity lacked caller validation, permission checks, and input sanitization, allowing any application to pass attacker-controlled data into the AI pipeline and trigger sensitive device-control operations through a privileged backend.

item.title: Arbitrary Content and URL Injection in Paypal via Deeplink
item.description: A content spoofing vulnerability exists due to unsanitized parameters, allowing in Arbitrary Text and URL injection in Paypal Android.

item.title: Arbitrary File Write and File Overwrite via Exposed JSBridge in Bing Android
item.description: The Bing Android application allows attacker-controlled URLs to be loaded via a deeplink into a WebView that exposes a JavaScript bridge to the loaded page.

item.title: Scam Shield Logic Flaw Enables Phishing Alert Spoofing for Any Sender ID or Number
item.description: A flaw in the Redacted app’s Scam Shield allows external Intents to trigger fake phishing alerts, letting malicious application or crafted deeplinks falsely flag legitimate sender IDs or phone numbers.

item.title: DOM-Based JavaScript Execution in Xiaomi Browser Reader Mode via <title> HTML Injection (Android)
item.description: A DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in Xiaomi Browser’s Read Mode due to insufficient sanitization of the HTML <title> tag, allowing arbitrary HTML or JavaScript to be executed via innerHTML.

item.title: Referrer Data Leakage in Facebook via Unvalidated data_uri Parameter
item.description: An open redirect vulnerability was discovered in Facebook’s Privacy Checkup endpoint due to the ?back_uri= parameter being processed without any security filtering, allowing attackers to redirect users to malicious website.

item.title: Linkshim Bypassed in Facebook Push Notication via Double URL Encoding
item.description: A persistent open redirect vulnerability was discovered in Facebook’s Push Notification endpoint due to improper validation of the ?ref= parameter, allowing attackers to redirect users to malicious sites and potentially facilitate phishing attacks.

item.title: Cross-Site Scripting in Opera Browser Reader Mode via Malicious <title> Tag (Android)
item.description: A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in Opera Browser for Android’s Reader Mode due to insufficient sanitization of the HTML <title> tag, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript, steal sensitive data, or inject malicious content

item.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass in OKX Android application via Exported WelcomeActivity
item.description: A broken multi-factor authentication vulnerability exists in OKX’s Android application due to an exported launcher Activity, allowing a locally installed malicious application to bypass the fingerprint-based multi-factor authentication check and resume a logged-in session without credentials.

item.title: Hacking Staysafe Philippines Contact Tracing Platform
item.description:
Key points of this writeup

  • Discovered a leaked OAuth token: StaySafe.ph’s Facebook login redirect exposed a long-lived (~59-day) access token directly in the URL. That token alone was enough to impersonate a user, no password required.
  • Reverse-engineered the mobile app: Decompiled ph.staysafe.mobileapp (v2.1) using Jadx and apktool to dig into how the app worked under the hood.
  • Accessed sensitive exposure data: With just the leaked token, pulled detailed contact-tracing logs showing exposure status (Probable, Suspect, Confirmed, Cleared, Initial), color-coded and dated, including full historical records, not just current data.
  • Mapped 20+ exposed API endpoints: Extracted from the app’s JS bundle, covering critical functions like password reset, OTP verification, account activation/deactivation, and account deletion.
  • Found an exposed, editable backend: The Laravel backend source and admin panel were publicly accessible, and editable, leaking massive amounts of PII for millions of users: names, emails, passwords, phone numbers, OTPs, vaccination status, locations, and more.

Technical Details

During the pandemic, I found vulnerabilities in the StaySafe Android application: a user location disclosure issue, a full account takeover via access token, and admin panel access exposing millions of users’ PII.
